packs.title: Capitol, Springs and Lake
packs.promise: Meet Austin through its state landmarks, art, spring-fed water and lakeside paths.

q.s: Use a museum object as the beginning of a sourced question.
st: Check current exhibition admission and choose an open display.
Notice two visible details in one object, then read its label.
Record one statement the label supports and a question it leaves you with.

q.s: Make a small personal response while crediting the artwork that prompted it.
st: Check current admission and visitor rules, then choose an open gallery.
Find a color relationship in one work and note the artist and title from its label.
Create an original small color study or written color description after moving to a permitted resting place.

q.s: Look at the setting of spring-fed water without entering it.
st: Check pool access and admission for the day.
From an open dry visitor position, find one natural edge and one built feature around the pool.
Read available city interpretation or its official ecology information and record one fact about the springs.

packs.title: South Congress in Small Details
packs.promise: Follow the avenue through music, roadside history and things made by hand.

q.s: Draw a small route using the clearest two cues.
st: Enter an open visitor shopping passage or observe its entrance from the sidewalk.
Find three cues showing where visitors can go: a directory, an opening and a change of surface.
Draw a small route using the clearest two cues.

q.s: Choose the pair with the strongest contrast and explain it in one line.
st: Remain on the public street sidewalk with a view of the hotel’s exterior.
Collect three material or shadow observations, describing only what you can see.
Choose the pair with the strongest contrast and explain it in one line.

q.t: A Message in Your Own Shape
q.s: Write your own short friendly message in a completely different layout; keep it in your notebook.
st: View the well-known wall from the public sidewalk without joining or blocking a photo line.
Notice how a simple message uses scale and empty space.
Write your own short friendly message in a completely different layout; keep it in your notebook.
